title: Beyond the Pocket, Against the Network

scenes.visual: Carried slate-blue (#4A90D9) kinase pocket on the left sits beside a smooth slate-blue K-Ras switch on the right holding amber-gold (#E8A838) GTP; crisp white title fades in at top: 'Beyond the Pocket, Against the Network' (labelled 'schematic').

scenes.tts: In the first film, imatinib won a kinase pocket and escape guided the next drug. Why did that plan fail for decades against the cancer switch K Ras? And how do networks push back even when a drug lands?
scenes.caption: In the first film, imatinib won a kinase pocket and escape guided the next drug. Why did that plan fail for decades against the cancer switch K-Ras? And how do networks push back even when a drug lands?
scenes.visual: Left side briefly shows teal (#2EC4B6) imatinib settled in slate-blue ABL; camera pans right onto slate-blue K-Ras gripping amber-gold GTP tightly as a teal drug block bounces off its smooth surface.
scenes.narration: In the first film, imatinib won a kinase pocket and escape guided the next drug. Why did that plan fail for decades against the cancer switch K-Ras? And how do networks push back even when a drug lands?

scenes.tts: The barrier is binding arithmetic. A ligand's share of a pocket scales with its concentration divided by its dissociation constant, the concentration that fills half the sites. For a typical kinase, one millimolar A T P divided by ten micromolar equals one hundred. A drug with a one-nanomolar constant, reaching one micromolar, scores one thousand. So the drug wins the pocket.
scenes.caption: The barrier is binding arithmetic. A ligand's share of a pocket scales with its concentration divided by its dissociation constant, the concentration that fills half the sites. For a typical kinase, 1 mM ATP divided by 10 µM equals 100. A drug with a 1 nM constant, reaching 1 µM, scores 1,000. So the drug wins the pocket.
scenes.visual: Formula appears crisp at top: 'Share scales with [ligand] / Kd'. Below, a computed occupancy bar for a kinase fills as each number appears in sync with speech: amber-gold ATP '1 mM / 10 µM = 100'; bright teal drug '1 µM / 1 nM = 1,000'; the teal drug bar claims ~91% of the pocket.
scenes.narration: The barrier is binding arithmetic. A ligand's share of a pocket scales with its concentration divided by its dissociation constant, the concentration that fills half the sites. For a typical kinase, 1 mM ATP divided by 10 µM equals 100. A drug with a 1 nM constant, reaching 1 µM, scores 1,000. So the drug wins the pocket.

scenes.tts: Now run that rule on K Ras. Cellular G T P sits near half a millimolar, while Ras holds it at about ten picomolar. Half a millimolar divided by ten picomolar is fifty million. A strong reversible drug at five micromolar, with a one-nanomolar constant, scores five thousand. That leaves barely one Ras in ten thousand holding the drug.
scenes.caption: Now run that rule on K-Ras. Cellular GTP sits near 0.5 mM, while Ras holds it at about 10 pM. 0.5 mM divided by 10 pM is 50,000,000. A strong reversible drug at 5 µM, with a 1 nM constant, scores 5,000. That leaves barely 1 Ras in 10,000 holding the drug.
scenes.visual: The computed occupancy bar shifts to K-Ras as each number appears in sync: amber-gold GTP '0.5 mM / 10 pM = 50,000,000' fills nearly 100% of the bar; bright teal drug '5 µM / 1 nM = 5,000' shrinks to a hairline sliver labelled '1 in 10,000'. The amber-gold GTP pocket stays completely locked.
scenes.narration: Now run that rule on K-Ras. Cellular GTP sits near 0.5 mM, while Ras holds it at about 10 pM. 0.5 mM divided by 10 pM is 50,000,000. A strong reversible drug at 5 µM, with a 1 nM constant, scores 5,000. That leaves barely 1 Ras in 10,000 holding the drug.

scenes.tts: Chemists stopped fighting G T P directly. One cancer mutation, G twelve C, replaces glycine twelve with cysteine. Cysteine exposes a reactive sulphur group called a thiol. Even mutant K Ras G twelve C still slowly cuts G T P to G D P, its off shape.
scenes.caption: Chemists stopped fighting GTP directly. One cancer mutation, G12C, replaces glycine 12 with cysteine. Cysteine exposes a reactive sulphur group called a thiol. Even mutant K-Ras G12C still slowly cuts GTP to GDP, its off shape.
scenes.visual: Zoom onto slate-blue K-Ras (schematic). A coral-red (#E05A47) tag labelled 'Cys 12 thiol' appears on the rim beside the nucleotide. Slowly, amber-gold GTP sheds a phosphate to become pale-gold GDP, and the protein shifts gently into its inactive conformation.
scenes.narration: Chemists stopped fighting GTP directly. One cancer mutation, G12C, replaces glycine 12 with cysteine. Cysteine exposes a reactive sulphur group called a thiol. Even mutant K-Ras G12C still slowly cuts GTP to GDP, its off shape.

scenes.tts: In that G D P shape, a hidden pocket opens beneath the switch two loop, beside the nucleotide site. Sotorasib enters and forms a permanent covalent bond to cysteine twelve. Normal Ras lacks cysteine twelve, so sotorasib spares it and never fights G T P.
scenes.caption: In that GDP shape, a hidden pocket opens beneath the switch II loop, beside the nucleotide site. Sotorasib enters and forms a permanent covalent bond to cysteine 12. Normal Ras lacks cysteine 12, so sotorasib spares it and never fights GTP.
scenes.visual: Beneath the lifted slate-blue loop labelled 'Switch II pocket', a cavity opens beside GDP. Bright teal sotorasib glides in and snaps a solid glowing bond onto coral-red Cys 12 ('Permanent covalent bond'). Beside it, normal K-Ras with no Cys 12 drifts untouched as teal sotorasib passes by.
scenes.narration: In that GDP shape, a hidden pocket opens beneath the switch II loop, beside the nucleotide site. Sotorasib enters and forms a permanent covalent bond to cysteine 12. Normal Ras lacks cysteine 12, so sotorasib spares it and never fights GTP.

scenes.tts: Other drugs sidestep natural active pockets too. Antibodies grab a receptor's outer face outside the cell. Allosteric inhibitors sit in a side pocket beside an enzyme's active site. They lock kinases such as Mek shut without displacing A T P.
scenes.caption: Other drugs sidestep natural active pockets too. Antibodies grab a receptor's outer face outside the cell. Allosteric inhibitors sit in a side pocket beside an enzyme's active site. They lock kinases such as MEK shut without displacing ATP.
scenes.visual: Camera pulls back to a schematic vertical signalling pathway across a cell membrane: Receptor -> Ras -> Raf -> MEK -> ERK. A teal Y-shaped antibody docks on the receptor's outer face ('Outside'); a teal allosteric block docks beside amber-gold ATP on slate-blue MEK ('Beside'); teal sotorasib stays locked on K-Ras ('Covalent').
scenes.narration: Other drugs sidestep natural active pockets too. Antibodies grab a receptor's outer face outside the cell. Allosteric inhibitors sit in a side pocket beside an enzyme's active site. They lock kinases such as MEK shut without displacing ATP.

scenes.tts: Yet every drug lands inside a living network. Remember: sotorasib traps K Ras G twelve C only in its brief G D P state. Pause and predict. If upstream growth receptors wake up and reload Ras with G T P, what happens to sotorasib's grip?
scenes.caption: Yet every drug lands inside a living network. Remember: sotorasib traps K-Ras G12C only in its brief GDP state. Pause and predict. If upstream growth receptors wake up and reload Ras with GTP, what happens to sotorasib's grip?
scenes.visual: On the schematic pathway, coral-red activation pulses travel down from the surface receptor toward K-Ras, carrying fresh amber-gold GTP tokens while teal sotorasib waits beside the switch II loop. Clean predict banner rises: 'Predict: What if receptors reload Ras with GTP?'
scenes.narration: Yet every drug lands inside a living network. Remember: sotorasib traps K-Ras G12C only in its brief GDP state. Pause and predict. If upstream growth receptors wake up and reload Ras with GTP, what happens to sotorasib's grip?

scenes.visual: The predict banner stays sharp while coral-red upstream arrows pulse steadily toward K-Ras and a smooth 4.5-second progress ring sweeps in the corner.

scenes.tts: Reloading G T P shrinks the G D P pool, so fewer Ras molecules get trapped. Networks push back in other ways. Block Mek, and Erk drops its braking signal, called negative feedback, so upstream steps push harder. Or cells amplify another receptor, like Met, to bypass the block.
scenes.caption: Reloading GTP shrinks the GDP pool, so fewer Ras molecules get trapped. Networks push back in other ways. Block MEK, and ERK drops its braking signal, called negative feedback, so upstream steps push harder. Or cells amplify another receptor, like MET, to bypass the block.
scenes.visual: Three rapid, clean schematic beats on the same carried pathway: (1) amber-gold GTP floods K-Ras, closing the switch II pocket; (2) on MEK inhibition, ERK's dashed brake line fades and coral-red bursts flare on receptor and Ras ('Feedback relieved'); (3) beside a blocked EGFR, three coral-red MET receptors appear and re-light the emerald-green (#4CAF50) downstream arrow ('Bypass').
scenes.narration: Reloading GTP shrinks the GDP pool, so fewer Ras molecules get trapped. Networks push back in other ways. Block MEK, and ERK drops its braking signal, called negative feedback, so upstream steps push harder. Or cells amplify another receptor, like MET, to bypass the block.

scenes.tts: That completes the map of targeted drugs. Side pockets, outer faces, and covalent bonds reach targets that beat reversible competition. Even then, blocking one part ripples through the whole circuit.
scenes.caption: That completes the map of targeted drugs. Side pockets, outer faces, and covalent bonds reach targets that beat reversible competition. Even then, blocking one part ripples through the whole circuit.
scenes.visual: The full carried schematic pathway holds briefly with teal drugs at outer face, side pocket, and mutant cysteine beside subtle coral-red feedback arrows, then fades cleanly into a dark slate backdrop.
scenes.narration: That completes the map of targeted drugs. Side pockets, outer faces, and covalent bonds reach targets that beat reversible competition. Even then, blocking one part ripples through the whole circuit.

scenes.visual: Clean full-frame end card on dark slate background showing one crisp white sentence only: 'New sites and covalent bonds bypass competition, yet networks push back.'
